item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Hiding behind that 5.00 ERA Emmet Sheehan toted around for much of the season might have been a valuable postseason piece.
Sheehan allowed just one hit in 5⅓ scoreless innings on Sunday afternoon as the Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants, 3-1, to complete a three-game sweep.
Sheehan retired 16 of the 18 batters he faced, allowing just one single and walking one while striking out nine.
“I’ve loved the version we’ve seen of Emmet the last three outings,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. “He’s been fantastic.
“We’ve seen confidence. We’ve seen when you’re essentially fighting for your life to create an opportunity for yourself. That’s what I see. There’s urgency. I like the way that he’s trusting his stuff. He’s in a good spot physically, and you know the performance has been fantastic.”
The outing was Sheehan’s third consecutive outstanding performance this month as he has bounced between Triple-A and the majors. It cemented a spot in the Dodgers’ postseason bullpen after a rough season for the 26-year-old right-hander – an outcome that did not seem likely when he was demoted to Triple-A in early August.
“I don’t know that I proved anything to myself. It was just getting a couple things right and I think I’m in a much better spot now,” Sheehan said.
“My confidence stayed the same the whole time. I knew the coaches down there were going to help me and I was going to get right. I took that approach going into it. I wasn’t helping the team here so I needed that a little bit.”
Sheehan has been called up for two starts this month and pitched in ‘bulk’ following Jack Dreyer as an opener on Sunday. Sheehan carried a 5.29 ERA into September after 20 starts for the Dodgers that landed him back in the minors.
In his three September outings, though, Sheehan has shown rediscovered fastball command after working on his delivery in Triple-A. He has allowed just one run in 17 innings, holding hitters to a .105 average (6 for 57) with 24 strikeouts and three walks. After giving up 20 home runs in those first 20 starts, he has allowed just one in his 17 September innings.
If his confidence didn’t need repair, his delivery and pitch mix needed some work.
Now two years removed from Tommy John surgery, Sheehan was thrown by not quite having recovered all of his fastball velocity this year. When he chased those extra miles per hour, it was counterproductive. He has become more comfortable at 94-95 mph now.
“I think it’s a few things,” he said Sunday. “Definitely … being more comfortable in my delivery, being out there staying free and easy with everything, not trying to do too much. Instead of saying, ‘I need 97 here.’ It’s more like ‘If I hit my spot, he’s not going to hit it.’”
They haven’t. Sheehan has gotten 50 swings-and-misses in his three outings this month, nearly half of them (24) on his reborn four-seam fastball. He also got six on his curveball on Sunday.
“That’s something that (assistant pitching coach) Connor (McGuinness), (pitching coach) Mark (Prior) and I and the coaches down in Triple-A have been working on is just expanding the front-to-back game with the fastball and the curveball,” Sheehan said. “I think some guys ended up throughout the season sitting mid-speed, slider-changeup, on me. Having that change of speeds the last couple has been very important.”
The Dodgers moved Sheehan to the bullpen for the postseason last October and saw him as a big weapon in that role. The results were mixed, however, in part because of some pitch tipping issues which Sheehan said have been addressed. He will be wiser this time around, he said.
“Definitely,” Sheehan said. “I think the routine of everything can be a little bit hard to adjust to right away. So having that experience helps a lot. Just getting back into that, I know what I need to do to get ready to go into the game.”
The Dodgers gave him a little bit of a test drive by using Dreyer as an ‘opener’ before him. The Giants scratched out one run in the first inning against Dreyer when he walked leadoff man Jonah Cox. Cox moved to second base on a wild pickoff attempt by Dreyer, stole third and scored on Victor Bericoto’s RBI single. The Giants had just one more hit in the game.
“I think that obviously there’s a 97 that plays better, but 94-95 commanded still misses bats,” Roberts said of Sheehan, who will rejoin Oklahoma City for the Triple-A playoffs this week before returning to the Dodgers for the postseason. “That’s one part of it. The other part of it is holding the velocity. And so, for me, the last three or four since he’s been back here, he’s held those 94s and 95s for the, call it 85 pitches.”
The Giants’ run against Dreyer stood up as the only run of the day until Tommy Edman emerged from a 2-for-41 slump to hit a solo home run in the sixth inning.
The Dodgers broke the 1-1 tie in the seventh on singles by Max Muncy and Josue De Paula followed by an RBI double from Kiké Hernandez.
They stranded De Paula and Hernandez in scoring position, but singles by Teoscar Hernandez, Freddie Freeman and Muncy produced another run in the eighth inning.
Kris Bubic, Brock Stewart and Tanner Scott combined on 2⅔ innings of hitless relief to close out the combined two-hitter for the Dodgers’ 96th win. With the win, the Dodgers’ magic number to clinch a first-round bye over the Atlanta Braves (who clinched the National League East division title on Sunday) dropped to three with six games left in the regular season.
The Dodgers (96-60) remain two games behind the Milwaukee Brewers (98-58) for the top seed, though the Brewers also hold the head-to-head tiebreaker. The No. 3 seed – currently Atlanta (92-64) – will play host to a best-of-three Wild Card Series against either the Chicago Cubs (87-69), San Diego Padres (87-69) or Philadelphia Phillies (86-70).

item.content:encoded:
Emmet Sheehan’s next start will be in the minor leagues.
The right-hander might be out of sight, but that doesn’t mean he will be out of mind.
His scheduled start Saturday for triple-A Oklahoma City in a Pacific Coast League playoff game is part of a design to prepare him to pitch for the Dodgers in October.
Sheehan has pitched his way into consideration for a spot on the playoff roster.
His quote-unquote demotion came after he pitched 5 ⅓ scoreless innings in the Los Angeles Dodgers’ sweep-sealing 3–1 victory over the San Francisco Giants Sunday.
The game was the third Sheehan pitched this month for the Dodgers. His numbers in those three games: 17 innings pitched, one run allowed, 24 strikeouts, three walks.
“I’ve loved the version we’ve seen of Emmet the last three outings,” manager Dave Roberts said. “He’s been fantastic.”
Sent down to Oklahoma City in early August, Sheehan returned to the major leagues earlier this month with a slightly modified arsenal that has significantly improved his results. He’s thrown his curveball more, and his increased inability to change speeds has made his fastball play up even when he’s not touching 97 mph with it.
“I think that obviously there’s a 97 that plays better, but 94–95 commanded still misses bats,” Roberts said. “So I think that’s something that, that’s one part of it. The other part of it is holding the velocity. And so, for me, the last three or four since he’s been back here, he’s held those 94s and 95s for the, call it, 85 pitches.”
With the Dodgers expecting to start Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell, Tarik Skubal and Tyler Glasnow in the postseason, the team has started the process of moving Sheehan into a relief role by having Jack Dreyer pitch an inning as opener Sunday. Sheehan was down in triple-A over the last week but a roster spot for him was opened up because Skubal went on the bereavement list.
Sheehan entered the game in the second inning and pitched into the seventh. He gave up only one hit and one walk; he struck out nine.
He said he has made it a point to feel “free and easy” with his delivery.
“Instead of saying, ‘I need 97 [mph] here,’ it’s more like, ‘If I hit my spot, he’s not going to hit it,’” Sheehan said.
What it means
The teams with the two-best records in each league will earn a first-round bye and the Dodgers are close to wrapping up one of those spots. With their win over the Giants, the Dodgers maintained a four-game lead over the Atlanta Braves for the National League’s No. 2 seed. Both teams have only six games remaining in the regular season.
Who’s hot
Left-hander Kris Bubic, who was acquired from the Kansas City Royals at the trade deadline, replaced Sheehan in the seventh inning and registered the final two outs of the inning. Bubic struck out Scott Bandura, only for Shay Whitcomb to reach base on a throwing error by Max Muncy.
No problem: Bubic forced Grant McCray to fly out to left field.
Bubic has pitched 2 ⅔ innings in three appearances for the Dodgers over the last week, and he still hasn’t allowed a run. He has struck out four.
Roberts said he’s also pitched his way into consideration for a spot on the playoff roster.
“It’s nothing overpowering, but there’s just funky swings, soft contact,” Roberts said. “I see him as a neutral pitcher, gets left and right out, and I like those converted starters because he knows how to navigate lineups.”
Who’s Not
For today, this section should be renamed “Who Wasn’t Hot.”
The label certainly applied to Tommy Edman, who was two for his last 42 before his sixth-inning at-bat: That’s when Edman jumped on an inside cutter from Carson Seymour and launched it into the visiting bullpen behind the right-field wall.
Edman’s home run tied the game at 1–1.
Up next
The Dodgers have a day off Monday. They will resume play Tuesday when they host the San Diego Padres, who will send No. 1 starter Michael King (12-9, 3.03 ERA) to the mound. The Dodgers won’t have a traditional starter, as Roberts said the team is planning for a bullpen game.

The Los Angeles Dodgers placed pitcher Tarik Skubal on the bereavement list on Sunday, which means he could miss his final regular-season turn in the rotation next week.
Skubal's next start is scheduled for Friday against the San Francisco Giants, which could fall within the three-to-seven days that players are allowed to be away from the team while on the bereavement list. But Dodgers manager Dave Roberts appeared to believe that Skubal will be back by Friday, telling reporters he would miss "a couple days."
"Some personal stuff going on, but he's fine," Roberts said, via MLB.com's Sonja Chen.
Skubal pitched in Saturday's 10-4 win over the Giants, allowing four runs and eight hits over five innings. He walked two batters with three strikeouts, tying his lowest total of the season. Saturday's game was the first time Skubal gave up more than three runs in his nine starts with the Dodgers. according to The Athletic's Fabian Ardaya.
Tarik Skubal pitched five innings and allowed four runs but is grateful for the offensive support.

LOS ANGELES — Kiké Hernández hit a go-ahead RBI double in the seventh inning, Emmet Sheehan did not give up a run in 5 1/3 innings, and the Los Angeles Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants 3-1 on Sunday to complete a three-game sweep.

Matt Wilkinson allowed three hits and no walks while striking out six in five scoreless innings, but the Giants’ bullpen buckled. The 23-year-old left-hander was acquired as part of the trade that sent catcher Patrick Bailey to Cleveland in May.
Tommy Edman homered to right in the sixth inning to tie the game at 1, tagging reliever Carson Seymour for the 400-foot shot.
Jonah Cox drew a leadoff walk to help spot the Giants their 1-0 lead. Cox reached second on a bad pickoff attempt by Dreyer before stealing third, and Victor Bericoto’s single drove him home.

Is it still a rivalry? Dodgers complete sweep of woeful Giants
- Click here to listen to this article
-
Only the Pirates and Cubs have met more often than the Dodgers and Giants, who faced off for the first time in 1889. And over all that time, the Dodgers are just two games better, with 1,294 wins to the Giants’ 1,292.
The Dodgers and Giants have also won more pennants, made more World Series appearances and have more players wearing their caps in the Hall of Fame than any other National League teams, all of which fueled a rivalry that was once among the most visceral and passionate in American sports.
But that was then and this is now.
After Sunday’s 3-1 victory over the Giants, the Dodgers’ 14th win in their last 17 games, the team could finish a season with 100 wins for the fourth time in six years. The Giants have had just one winning record in that time.
The Dodgers (96-60), who have won five straight division titles, are headed to the postseason for a record-tying 14th consecutive year. The Giants will miss the playoffs for a fifth straight season.
So is the rivalry dead? That depends on who you ask.
“It’s always a rivalry,” Giants pitcher Logan Webb. “We’d like to make it a little closer when it comes to the standings. But I definitely feel it when I throw against them.”
But then Webb, who is from Northern California, grew up with the rivalry and, as the longest-tenured Giant, pitched against the Dodgers in games that mattered. Giants coach Ron Washington, who made his major league debut with the Dodgers when the rivalry was still a thing, said many players on San Francisco’s roster don’t know that background.
Mookie Betts hits three doubles and the Dodgers piled up 15 hits in a 10-4 win over the San Francisco Giants with Shohei Ohtani’s return on the horizon.
“It should be a rivalry. But I don’t think the young kids we got know anything about a rivalry. They’re not history buffs.”
Webb said it’s the responsibility of the veterans on both sides to keep that history alive by explaining the enmity to the young players.
“I think there are still guys that came up in the system that know what it’s like,” he said. “It’s my job to kind of hype these guys up to play a game like this.”
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts, who played for the Dodgers and Giants during his 10-year career, agrees the rivalry now exists more in the history books than the current standings, where the Giants have been overtaken by the San Diego Padres, who will finish second to the Dodgers in the N.L. West for the fourth time in five seasons.
“It’s certainly a rivalry in the sense of the history, the fan bases,” Roberts said. “But obviously it’s about relevancy. The Padres have been successful the last handful of years, and so it’s certainly built some momentum. The geography lends itself to that too.
“But Dodgers Giants is always fun.”
It hasn’t been so much fun for the Giants lately. San Francisco hasn’t won the season series with the Dodgers since 2021 and has lost more than 90 games this year for the first time in nine seasons.
On Sunday they went in front three batters into the game with Johan Cox working Dodger opener Jack Dreyer for a leadoff walk, then making his way around the bases on Dreyer’s throwing error, a stolen base and a one-one single by Victor Bericoto.
But San Francisco didn’t get another hit until Jung Hoo Lee singled with one out in the sixth.
That allowed the Dodgers to tie the score in the sixth on Tommy Edman’s seventh home run of the season just inside the right-field foul pole. An inning later they went ahead to stay when Max Muncy singled under a sliding Cox at second, moved to third on a single by rookie Josue De Paula and scored on Kiké Hernández’s double to center.
A two-out single by Muncy, his second of the game, scored Teoscar Hernández, who also had two hits, in the eighth inning with the final run.
Even the slumping Freddie Freeman contributed to the Dodgers’ 11-hit attack, ending an 0-for-11 slide with a broken-bat single in the fourth then singling again in the eighth.
Sunday’s result helped clarify the Dodgers’ once-muddy playoff picture. With six games left in the regular season, the Dodgers lead Atlanta by four games in the race for the second seed in the National League playoffs, which would give them a first-round bye and the homefield advantage in the division series.
The team’s postseason roster may be getting clearer as well. Right-hander Emmet Sheehan, who made 22 starts this season, came out of the bullpen for the first time Sunday and was brilliant in his audition for the playoffs.
“If there is a role in the postseason, it will be out of the [bull]pen,” Roberts said of Sheehan, who gave up just a hit and walk, striking out nine — one off his season high — in 5 1/3 innings.
Tyler Glasnow hasn’t had the greatest of seasons, but the Dodgers will need him to deliver in the playoffs if they want to win another World Series title.
De Paula, meanwhile, who also doubled in running his modest hitting streak to four games, appears to have secured a job as the team’s left-handed bat off the bench while utility player Hyeseong Kim, who has spent the last four months in the minors, will rejoin the Dodgers after the triple-A playoffs and be considered for a roster spot as a pinch-runner and late-inning defensive replacement.
“My expectation is that Hyeseong will be here during the off week and potentially be a conversation for the postseason because he has the ability to run, play defense, and steal a base,” Roberts said.
After Monday’s off day, the final break of the regular season for the Dodgers, the team is expected to activate Andy Pages, Roki Sasaki and Shohei Ohtani from the injured list during its three-game series with the Padres.

The Los Angeles Dodgers took a 3-1 win in their series finale against the San Francisco Giants on Sunday, finishing a three-game sweep.
The Dodgers had a scheduled bullpen day on Sunday, but Emmet Sheehan handled most of the pitching. He had arguably his best outing of the season, completely shutting down the Giants over the course of his 5.1-inning performance.
He only allowed one hit and one walk, keeping the Giants from scoring while striking out nine batters on the afternoon.
The right-hander is putting together a serious case to make the postseason roster, allowing just one earned run over his last 17 innings pitched while striking out 24 batters.
Sheehan entered the game trailing, though, as Jack Dreyer allowed a run in the opening inning of the game. Jonah Cox took full advantage of a walk, advancing to second base on a throwing error before stealing third base. He came around to score on a Victor Bericoto single.
The Dodgers scattered baserunners over the course of the next several innings, and finally made a breakthrough in the sixth inning.
Tommy Edman took full advantage of an inside cutter, hitting his seventh homer of the season to tie the game.
The Dodgers scored yet again in the seventh inning, as both Max Muncy and Josue De Paula singled to put two on with just one out.
Kiké Hernandez stepped up to the plate, doubling into the gap in right-center field to bring home Muncy and give the Dodgers the lead.
They scored yet again in the eighth inning, as Teoscar Heranndez and Freddie Freeman both singled to bring Muncy to the plate. He came through yet again for the Dodgers, adding some insurance heading into the ninth inning.
Tanner Scott came in for the ninth inning, and got out without allowing a run despite a walk early in the frame.
The Dodgers get an off day Monday before heading into a three-game series against the San Diego Padres, which begins Tuesday at 7:10 p.m. PT.

Repeating the trend of these series’ first two games, the Dodgers didn’t take the lead until the second half of the game—this time keeping their scoring to nearly the minimum needed to overcome the Giants, sweeping their rivals with a 3-1 victory that relied heavily on Emmet Sheehan’s work as the bulk man, following Jack Dreyer.
Better late than never: Dodgers offense pounces on the Giants’ bullpen in win
Emmet Sheehan’s outstanding work as a follower allowed the Dodgers to beat the Giants with just three runs
Without putting the ball in play, the Giants placed a man on third in the opening inning, manufacturing a run partially thanks to Dreyer’s loose grip on the running game. Leadoff hitter Jonah Cox earned a walk as Dreyer struggled to locate his heater, moved to second on an errant pickoff attempt, and aggressively stole third—hardly a surprise for a rookie with 13 stolen bases in just 140 plate appearances. Cox was driven in by a Jonah Bericoto single, a run that would loom large given the effectiveness of both Sheehan and Giants starter Matt Wilkinson.
Deceptive with his low-90s fastball that gets terrific results, Giants starter Matt Wilkinson didn’t encounter many problems holding the Dodgers scoreless through five innings of work. Only twice did Wilkinson need to strand one-out doubles, but on both occasions with minimal stress. That success was at least partially owed to a lefty-heavy lineup—three of the four outs Wilkinson recorded with a runner in scoring position came against a left-handed hitter, but then again, one of the doubles came from Josue De Paula, so we mustn’t read too much into it.
As soon as Wilkinson got the hook, though, the Dodgers would tie the game in the bottom of the sixth, thanks to a solo shot from Tommy Edman off Carson Seymour. Traditionally a better power hitter from the right side, Edman was looking in the whole way and crushed one all the way out to the Giants’ bullpen.
The only reason why the Dodgers were able to tie the score with just one swing was the fact that Sheehan matched Wilkinson pitch for pitch and then some. Overall, few players have improved their case for a significant postseason role over the past couple of weeks with the Dodgers quite like Sheehan, a new pitcher since his return following a one-month stint in Triple-A. Pitching as brilliantly as he did in two September starts, Sheehan completely shut down the Giants’ lineup through 5.1 innings, enjoying great success with a curveball that induced six whiffs on 12 swings, leading him to strike out nine batters.
Proving Wilkinson and his difficult-to-pick-up fastball were the problem, the Dodgers’ offense scored again in the seventh—they took the lead thanks to a Kiké Hernández RBI single after De Paula and Max Muncy set the table despite an unfavorable matchup against the southpaw.
Mookie Betts nearly put this game to bed, but what would’ve been a two-out, three-run bomb died at the wall, leaving the score at 2-1. The Dodgers would still find a way to provide a little cushion to Tanner Scott in the ninth inning, adding one more run in the bottom of the eighth thanks to a Max Muncy two-out RBI single.

Although neither team has announced their starters, based on the current schedule, the first game of that series would pit Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Robbie Ray against each other. LOS ANGELES -- Before Sunday’s game, the Los Angeles Dodgers made several roster moves, recalling right-handed pitchers Emmet Sheehan and Kyle Hurt while optioning right-hander Seth Halvorsen. The club also placed left-hander Tarik Skubal on the bereavement list.
The Dodgers would go on to win 3-1, with Kris Bubic recording the victory for his fourth win of the season.
Giants rookie starter Matt Wilkinson kept the Dodgers in check for most of his outing, pitching five shutout innings while striking out six. He consistently kept the Dodgers’ lineup off balance and prevented them from generating much offensively.
For the Dodgers, however, the pitching staff put together a complete performance outside of the one run allowed by Jack Dreyer. Sheehan followed Dreyer and delivered an especially effective outing in his return to the roster.
The right-hander pitched 5.1 innings, allowing just one hit while striking out eight. Considering the struggles Sheehan has endured throughout the 2026 season, seeing him throw the ball this effectively was particularly encouraging after the many setbacks he has faced.
The outing also builds on what Sheehan did in his previous appearance on Sept. 13 against the Miami Marlins. He pitched six scoreless innings while striking out five before being optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City the following day. The Dodgers recalled him Sunday, and he immediately followed that previous performance with another strong showing.
It wasn’t until the sixth inning that the Dodgers finally got on the board. Tommy Edman hit a solo home run to right field, and Kiké Hernández followed with an RBI double in the seventh to give the Dodgers a 2-1 lead. The Dodgers would add additional insurance in the eighth when Max Muncy delivered an RBI single to give the Dodgers their final run of the game and a 3-1 lead.
Bubic also made an appearance, marking his second game with the Dodgers and his first at Dodger Stadium. He took over for Sheehan after the first out of the sixth inning and recorded the final two outs, striking out one of the two batters he faced.
Bubic, an All-Star in 2025, joined the Dodgers after being acquired at the trade deadline in August. Previously with the Kansas City Royals, Bubic carved out a role as one of the better left-handed starters in the American League while also proving capable of working out of the bullpen throughout his career.
That versatility is exactly what the Dodgers hope he can provide. The expectation is that Bubic could serve as a high-leverage reliever out of the bullpen once October arrives. His role could look similar to the one Justin Wrobleski had during the Dodgers’ 2025 playoff push, when Wrobleski was used as a reliever capable of covering multiple innings while remaining an effective arm.
Those plans have yet to be finalized, but Bubic’s previous experience gives the Dodgers another option to consider. The hope is that he can provide some stability to the bullpen during the final weeks of the regular season before the Dodgers determine their postseason roster.

Los Angeles Dodgers shortstop Mookie Betts led off in manager Dave Roberts' lineup for the third consecutive game Sunday against the San Francisco Giants. Betts looks immovable right now, especially on the heels of a game in which he reached base five times. He collected three doubles, a single and a walk in the Dodgers' 10-4 win on Saturday at Dodger Stadium.
Betts' September surge marks an abrupt change from the five months that came before.
Through the end of August, Betts' .701 OPS ranked 123rd out of 163 major league hitters with at least 400 plate appearances. Since Sept. 1, his OPS was an outstanding 1.287 entering Sunday, trailing only Cincinnati Reds shortstop Elly De La Cruz among 181 qualified hitters this month.
"I couldn’t tell you that I saw this,” Roberts said Saturday, referring to Betts' dramatic turnaround. “But I just felt that he was stronger. He’s worked hard on that. He looks great. He’s not going to stop working, and just for it to come together has been great.”
The Dodgers will have a choice to make if and when Shohei Ohtani returns from the injured list. Ostensibly he'll go back to the leadoff spot again, though his health — and Betts' resurgence — are at least making it a conversation.
For the Dodgers, it's a good problem to have at the right time.
At 33, Betts is facing many of the same questions the Dodgers' other 30-and-over stars face anytime their performance slips. Has age caught up to them? Can they maintain their performance through the end of October? Do the Dodgers need a younger player to take their place in order to repeat as World Series champions?
The questions apply to Miguel Rojas (37), Freddie Freeman (36), Max Muncy (35), Kiké Hernández (34), Teoscar Hernández (33), Tommy Edman (31) and Ohtani (31), as well as Betts.
Professional athletes are famously the last to know when their physical skills are no longer enough to justify their roster spot. Take it with a grain of salt, but Betts isn't worried about his ability to maintain his current stretch of play.
“I mean this is it,” Betts said of his recent form. “I know I’m still capable of it, it’s in there somewhere. So, just gotta keep on rolling, keep on laying the foundation and letting the game be the game.”

LOS ÁNGELES.— Mookie Betts bateó de 4-4 con tres dobles, Will Smith agregó tres hits, incluyendo un jonrón, y los Dodgers de Los Ángeles vencieron a los Gigantes de San Francisco 10-4 el sábado por la noche.
El sencillo de dos carreras con dos outs de Tommy Edman ante el relevista Philip Abner rompió el empate a 4 en la quinta entrada. El bateador emergente Miguel Rojas conectó un sencillo productor para poner el marcador 7-4 a favor de su equipo, y Edman fue puesto out en el plato para finalizar la entrada.
Todos los Dodgers conectaron al menos un hit, excepto Freddie Freeman, quien tuvo un mal desempeño y se fue de 0 de 5. Betts igualó su mejor marca de la temporada en hits y el equipo superó a los Giants en jonrones, 15-8. El ex Jugador Más Valioso de la Liga Americana bateaba .249 hace una semana y desde entonces ha elevado su promedio a .261.
Los Dodgers anotaron carreras en seis entradas consecutivas al inicio de un partido por primera vez en 10 años. Han anotado 15 carreras en sus últimas siete entradas ofensivas, incluyendo cuatro jonrones en la octava entrada contra Abner en el primer partido de la serie del viernes.
Los campeones de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional (95-60) ganaron su partido número 95 para colocarse 35 juegos por encima del .500, su mejor marca de la temporada.
El tercer doble de Betts abrió la sexta entrada y anotó con un sencillo productor de Smith ante el relevista Joel Kuhnel. El novato Josue De Paula añadió un sencillo productor de dos carreras, ampliando la ventaja a 10-4.
En tres ocasiones, los Giants remontaron para empatar el partido, solo para ver cómo los Dodgers volvían a tomar la delantera, destacando el jonrón de dos carreras de Victor Bericoto, de 425 pies, que empató el partido en la tercera entrada.
El abridor de los Dodgers, Tarik Skubal (11-7), no estuvo especialmente brillante, permitiendo cuatro carreras y ocho hits en cinco entradas. El zurdo ponchó a tres y otorgó dos bases por bolas, y los Dodgers ganaron sus últimas seis salidas.
El relevista Edwin Díaz lanzó una octava entrada sin permitir carreras en su segunda aparición consecutiva desde que salió de la lista de lesionados el viernes.
El abridor de los Giants, Yunior Marte (0-1), permitió seis carreras y ocho hits en 4 2/3 entradas con dos ponches.
El jardinero derecho de los Dodgers, Kyle Tucker, recibió un foul en la rodilla y fue reemplazado por Alex Call en la séptima entrada.

20 Sep 2026, 13:49 GMT+10

Pinch hitter Pavin Smith hit a two-run, walk-off homer with one out in the ninth and the Arizona Diamondbacks beat the New York Yankees 5-3 on Saturday in Phoenix on a night the franchise celebrated the 25th anniversary of their 2001 World Series victory over the Yankees.
Ildemaro Vargas walked to lead off the ninth off Michael Fulmer (0-1), reaching base after he appealed the 3-2 pitch that originally was called a strike. After a strikeout, Smith hit a 391-foot homer to right center for the D-backs' 46th comeback win of the season
Heliot Ramos and Austin Wells hit bases-empty homers for the Yankees, who had won four of five and eight of 10. Wells and Jose Caballero had two hits apiece.
Nolan Arenado had two hits and Jordan Lawlar added a two-run triple for the D-backs, who had lost three in a row and five of six.
The Yankees (89-65), who have clinched a playoff berth, fell five games behind Tampa Bay (94-60) in the American League East and remained 5 1/2 games ahead of Boston (84-71) for the top AL wild-card spot. The Yankees and Rays play a four-game series in Yankee Stadium beginning with a split doubleheader Tuesday.
White Sox 3, Tigers 1
Sean Burke hurled six quality innings and Miguel Vargas homered to help Chicago earn a victory over visiting Detroit.
Burke (10-7) allowed one run on five hits for Chicago, which remained a game behind American League Central-leading Cleveland. Sam Antonacci and Munetaka Murakami both drove in a run and Grant Taylor delivered a four-out save, his 10th overall this season.
Jackson Jobe (2-3) threw six innings of three-run, four-hit ball, striking out nine for Detroit, which remains barely alive in AL Central contention. The Tigers' wild-card elimination magic number is down to one. Kevin McGonigle drove in Detroit's lone run.
Mets 10, Phillies 3
Francisco Alvarez had two hits, including the go-ahead three-run homer in the fifth, as host New York routed skidding Philadelphia.
Carson Benge was 3-for-4 with a solo homer and two RBIs for the Mets. Brett Baty had two hits, including a run-scoring single, while Benge, Juan Soto and Bo Bichette each had RBI singles during a four-run eighth.
Alec Bohm had RBI singles in the fourth and fifth for the Phillies, who missed a chance to take over the top National League wild card, at least temporarily. The Cubs and Padres both won to remain tied atop the NL wild-card race.
Brewers 1, Orioles 0Robert Gasser pitched seven shutout innings as the first of three Milwaukee pitchers in a victory against host Baltimore.
It marked the second shutout for Milwaukee pitchers in an eight-game stretch, needing only four strikeouts for the latest accomplishment. The Brewers scored on Gary Sanchez's second-inning groundout to knock in Joey Ortiz, who tripled with one out.Baltimore has lost the first two games of the series following a three-game winning streak, further damaging its American League playoff hopes. Orioles starter Trevor Rogers (10-11) lasted eight innings, allowing one run and three hits.
Rangers 6, Blue Jays 2Texas won for the sixth time in its past seven games, defeating Toronto in Arlington, Texas.Rangers starting pitcher Cal Quantrill left the game after 1 1/3 innings with right lat tightness. Jordan Montgomery (1-0) replaced him and held Toronto hitless through 3 2/3 innings. Josh Jung gave Texas a 1-0 lead in the bottom of the first with a home run to right field.Jose Soriano (12-8) gave up six runs (five earned) on four hits and struck out eight in five-plus innings for the Blue Jays, who dropped to three games behind the Chicago White Sox for the final wild-card berth in the American League.
Rays 2, Red Sox 1
Richie Palacios produced a two-out, walk-off single in the ninth inning as Tampa Bay edged Boston in St. Petersburg, Fla., to even their final home series of the regular season.
Against Garrett Whitlock (7-2), Palacios looped a 1-2 sinker into right to score Junior Caminero as the Rays hit their third walk-off winner during their nine-game homestand. Jonathan Aranda homered while Liam Hicks and Chandler Simpson posted two hits apiece.
Caleb Durbin stroked two doubles and scored for the Red Sox, who lost for the first time in three games. Starting pitcher Brayan Bello went a season-best eight innings and allowed one run on five hits with a career high-tying 11 strikeouts.
Guardians 12, Athletics 6
Angel Martinez homered from both sides of the plate and drove in four runs in host Cleveland's win over the Athletics which helped maintain its one-game lead in the American League Central.
Martinez was also 4-for-5 with a double and three runs scored and Chase DeLauter also homered for the Guardians, who won their fourth straight. Slade Cecconi (5-7) got the win in relief with two scoreless innings after Tanner Bibee lasted 4 2/3 innings and surrendered six runs on 12 hits.
Donovan Walton hit a home run and was 3-for-3 with four RBIs for the Athletics, who have lost five in a row. Athletics starter and loser Jacob Lopez (6-5) was blitzed for 10 runs and 10 hits in 2 2/3 innings.
Nationals 8, Cardinals 5 (11 innings)Jose Tena's two-run double keyed a four-run 11th inning and Washington beat the Cardinals in St. Louis.Jorbit Vivas had four hits and Daylen Lile homered for Washington, which has won six of seven. Riley Cornelio (3-2) pitched 1 2/3 innings for the win.At the top of the order, Jose Fermin and Ivan Herrera had three hits each for St. Louis, which has lost four straight.
Cubs 5, Reds 2
Michael Busch and Dansby Swanson hit solo home runs to lift visiting Chicago to a win over Cincinnati.
The win allowed the Cubs to pull a full game ahead of the Philadelphia Phillies for the top wild-card playoff spot in the National League. The Phillies lost 10-3 to the Mets earlier. The San Diego Padres also won to remain tied with the Cubs.
The teams will play the rubber game of the series Sunday. Cubs starter Matthew Boyd (9-5) gave up two hits and two runs (one earned) in five innings. Reds starter Nick Lodolo (3-6) gave up seven hits and three runs in seven innings.
Pirates 6, Royals 5
Brandon Lowe launched a go-ahead two-run home run in the eighth inning to power Pittsburgh to a victory over visiting Kansas City.
Ronny Simon and Jake Mangum each hit two-run homers, while Oneil Cruz, Rafael Flores Jr. and Lowe each had two hits for the Pirates. Right-hander Luke Weaver (3-1) threw a scoreless eighth with one strikeout, and left-hander Mason Montgomery earned his 15th save of the season after working around a walk with one strikeout in a scoreless ninth.
Nick Loftin had four hits, while Bobby Witt Jr. went 3-for-5 with two runs and extended his on-base streak to 17 games for the Royals. Carter Jensen hit a solo homer, while Jac Caglianone and Vinnie Pasquantino each had two hits for Kansas City.
Braves 6, Astros 3Ronald Acuna Jr. hit a grand slam, Grant Holmes produced a quality start and Atlanta lowered its magic number to one to clinch the National League East by defeating host Houston.The Braves secured this three-game interleague series and set the table to win the NL East for the seventh time in nine seasons with a victory in the series finale on Sunday. Holmes (10-5) allowed two runs on eight hits over six innings. Closer Raisel Iglesias notched his 34th save for Atlanta.The Astros dropped a game behind the Rangers in the AL West after Texas beat Toronto. Astros reliever AJ Blubaugh (5-3) loaded the bases and was replaced by Bryan Abreu, who gave up Acuna's homer in the seventh inning for a 5-2 Braves lead.Rockies 5, Mariners 3
Cole Carrigg delivered a go-ahead two-run single in a four-run seventh inning as Colorado edged Seattle in Denver.

The Padres tied the Chicago Cubs for the top wild-card spot in the National League at 86-69. Miami forced extra innings when pinch hitter Griffin Conine pulled a 102 mph fastball from closer Mason Miller for a game-tying homer with one out in the ninth.

Betts has 10 hits over his past three games, including seven in the past two while operating out of the leadoff spot in place of an injured Shohei Ohtani. Will Smith homered as the Dodgers won for the fifth time in six games and improved to 13-3 since Sept. 3. Tarik Skubal (11-7) gave up four runs on eight hits over five innings.
Victor Bericoto hit a home run among his two hits for the Giants while Yunior Marte (0-1) gave up six runs on eight hits over 4 2/3 innings in his fourth career appearance and second start.

LOS ANGELES — Mookie Betts is showing that the view from the top offers a wide range of possibilities.
Hitting in Shohei Ohtani’s leadoff spot for the second consecutive game, Betts’ four-hit performance on Saturday night topped his three-hit output from Friday and started some serious downhill momentum toward a 10-4 victory over the San Francisco Giants.
The victory kept the Dodgers (95-60) two games behind the Milwaukee Brewers (97-58) for the best record in the National League and four games ahead of the Atlanta Braves (91-64) for the No. 2 playoff seed with seven games remaining. That includes four games against the Giants, who continue to limp toward the finish line of a miserable, injury-riddled season.
Betts couldn’t be feeling better, with his past two games part of a run of 10 hits over the last three games he has played. After more than two months of looking for an offensive leader, Betts has charged into the role, while reaching base five times on Saturday.
“It’s good; It’s fun,” Betts said. “But the main thing is doing it when it counts. So right now, we just keep laying the foundation, and then when playoffs come, we just need it to show up (offensively).”
The Dodgers expect Ohtani to return for the playoffs as he makes progress from biceps and knee discomfort. Betts, though, is proving to be a more-than-adequate emergency replacement.
“You know, I couldn’t tell you that I saw this (coming), but I just felt that he was stronger,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. “He’s worked hard on that. He looks great. He’s not going to stop working, and just for it to come together has been great, and I think for me it’s just trying to keep him confident.”
The Dodgers also have been transformed by the emergence of catcher Will Smith, who returned at the start of September after three months away because of neck inflammation. He had a home run among his three hits Saturday to give him homers in consecutive games, with three over his past eight contests.
“He’ll play two or three that last series (at San Francisco), but yeah, after that, he’ll be our guy (for the playoffs),” Roberts said.
There is also 21-year-old rookie Josue De Paula, who has continued to operate with ease since arriving in the major leagues last week. De Paula had a two-run single Saturday and walked twice while scoring two runs.
All of it overshadowed Tarik Skubal’s ninth start for the Dodgers. The two-time American League Cy Young Award winner was far from his best, allowing four runs on eight hits over five innings. His three strikeouts were his least in an outing with his new club.
Skubal unleashed his frustrations in the dugout by throwing his glove and cap at the bench, while firing an empty sports drink bottle at the wall.
“Sometimes you get frustrated and you got to get it out,” Skubal said. “It’s no good just keeping it pent up. So yeah, I’m a believer in getting that stuff out and kind of just moving on from the moment. The frustration is based on execution and knowing who I am and I’m just not doing that.”
Skubal blamed a lack of fastball command for the inability to shut down the Giants.
“Not driving it up and in (and) kind of pulling the ball down at times, pushing it up at times,” Skubal said. “I think pitching is almost all fastball command and mine wasn’t great today.”
And yet the offense allowed Skubal (11-7) to pick up the win, while improving to 4-2 with a 2.95 ERA for the Dodgers.
“That’s our job. That’s what we’re supposed to do,” Betts said. “So sometimes it’s them, sometimes it’s us. As long as we win.”
Kyle Tucker provided a scare when he fouled a ball off the side of his right knee early in the game then departed in the seventh inning with the Dodgers leading by six runs. Tucker reached base twice Saturday after collecting six hits with two home runs the previous two games.
“Whatever’s working at the time, you just ride it out, whether or not it’s the way you want to go about it,” said Tucker, who expects to play Sunday. “If it’s working, it’s working. You just try to go up there and put up competitive at-bats and just do your part on defense.”
The offense was not only productive, it was steady. The Dodgers scored runs in each of the first six innings and when they were held scoreless in the seventh, Betts still reached base with a walk.
Betts opened the game for the Dodgers with a leadoff double and scored on a Max Muncy double. Betts brought home his own run with an RBI single in the second.
The Dodgers struck with Smith’s home run in the third and got an RBI double from Betts in the fourth but were still tied 4-4 heading into the bottom of the fifth. They blew the game open from there, getting a go-ahead two-run single from Tommy Edman and an RBI pinch-hit single from Miguel Rojas for a 7-4 lead.
They scored three more times in the sixth, getting a Smith RBI single followed by a two-run single from De Paula.
“I think this is the first time, seems like all year, that we’ve had four or five hitters swing the bats well for four or five games,” Roberts said. “So it’s been really good to see. Obviously, Mookie is a big part of it, but everyone else is doing their part.”
The Dodgers now have a 5-4 lead in the Giants in the season series and are in line for a sweep on Sunday, which would be their first against their longtime rival since April of 2024.

LOS ANGELES -- Mookie Betts went 4 for 4 with three doubles, Will Smith added three hits including a home run, and the Los Angeles Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants 10-4 on Saturday night.
Tommy Edman's two-run, two-out single off reliever Philip Abner snapped a 4-all tie in the fifth. Pinch-hitter Miguel Rojas followed with an RBI single for a 7-4 lead, with Edman thrown out at home to end the inning.

The Dodgers scored runs in six straight innings to start a game for the first time in 10 years. They've scored 15 runs in their last seven offensive innings, including a four-homer eighth off Abner in Friday's series opener.
The NL West champions (95-60) won their 95th game to move a season-high 35 games above .500.
Betts' third double led off the sixth and he scored on Smith's RBI single off reliever Joel Kuhnel. Rookie Josue De Paula added a two-run RBI single, extending the lead to 10-4.
Three times the Giants rallied to tie the game only to see the Dodgers retake the lead, highlighted by Victor Bericoto's game-tying, 425-foot two-run homer in the third.

Plan A, as always, is Shohei Ohtani.
But over the last couple nights, Plan B has looked pretty good too.
Whenever Ohtani returns from the injured list, the two-way star will likely reprise his customary role as the Dodgers’ leadoff hitter –– one he has held since halfway through his debut 2024 season with the team.
Likely, however, was as far as manager Dave Roberts was willing to describe it on Saturday.
Because in Ohtani’s absence, Mookie Betts has made a case to spearhead the team’s order, too.
Over the last week, a red-hot Betts has served as the Dodgers’ leadoff hitter three times. In each of those contests, he delivered a vintage performance.
There was a 2-for-4 display with an RBI and a double in Miami last week.
A 3-for-4 outburst with two home runs (including one to lead off the game) against the San Francisco Giants on Friday night.
Then, a 4-for-4, three-double, two-RBI, one-walk masterpiece in another 10-4 rout of the Giants on Saturday, a victory that lowered the Dodgers’ magic number to clinch a first-round playoff bye down to four with eight days remaining in the season.
“I just think he’s physically in a better spot than he has been,” Roberts said after Saturday’s outburst, which pushed Betts’ season average up to .261 and OPS to .785. “The ball’s coming off the right way.”
Of course, Betts has been crushing the ball regardless of where he’s been in the order lately. Since Aug. 5, he is batting .336 in 39 games with nine home runs, 12 doubles, 31 RBIs and a 1.008 OPS.
It has marked the former MVP’s best extended stretch since early in the 2024 season. It has been a reminder that there’s still plenty of life left in his previously slumping bat.
“I know I’m still capable of it,” the 33-year-old Betts said. “I know it was in there somewhere.”
Added Roberts: “It just doesn’t matter where you hit him, who he’s facing, [what’s] the situation –– he’s taking good at-bats.”
Betts’ impact at the top of the lineup specifically, however, has been impossible to ignore over the last week; especially when juxtaposed with the ongoing uncertainty surrounding Ohtani, who is expected back next week from right arm and left knee injuries but still doesn’t figure to be 100% physically.
That’s why, after writing Betts’ name in at the leadoff spot for a second-straight day Saturday, Roberts was asked if it’s still a certainty that Ohtani will remain in the leadoff spot upon his return.
“Yeah, I mean, I think that’s my first kind of thought,” Roberts said. “But until he gets back, or when he gets back, then I’ll kind of potentially read and react.”
Much will obviously depend on how Ohtani looks, which will be the biggest question after a 6-for-52 slump leading up to his IL stint.
Roberts also cited other factors like trying to match up against either right- or left-handed pitching, leaving the door open to some game-by-game tinkering in October.
“I haven’t really thought too much about it [yet],” he insisted.
The way Betts is going, though, it might soon become a critical lineup-construction decision.
Run the risk with a potentially diminished but ever-dangerous Ohtani? Or give the most at-bats as possible to the team’s hottest current hitter?
Granted, Betts hasn’t pushed to take over the leadoff spot, saying Friday that “I’ll hit wherever” and “there’s a guy that’s named Shohei that needs to be up there and to get us going.”
But if the Dodgers need to pivot among Ohtani’s ongoing ailments, he is quickly emerging as their best fallback option –– especially with their initial leadoff replacement, the switch-hitting Tommy Edman, mired in a brutal 2-for-39 slump.
“Going back up there, it is fun,” Betts acknowledged, having played almost 1,100 career games as a leadoff hitter over his 13-year career. “Kind of feels like home.”
“You do got to kind of prepare for whatever,” Roberts added, “and I just think that Mookie’s swinging the bat well, has hit there many times throughout his career, so it just kind of makes sense.”
For now, the Dodgers’ bigger priority will be making sure Betts keeps swinging the bat well, whether that’s in the No. 1 spot or somewhere else in the heart of the order.
His late-season surge has been one of the biggest reasons the team has survived Ohtani’s absence –– winning 13 of its last 16 despite the superstar slugger playing in just one of those contests.
“It’s good. It’s fun. But the main thing is doing it when it counts,” Betts said of his recent success. “Right now, just keep laying the foundation, and then when playoffs come, just need it to show up.”
Still, given how things are trending at the moment, it might not be a surprise if the Dodgers’ first at-bat of the playoffs belonged to their streaking shortstop.
“I couldn’t tell you that I saw this [coming],” Roberts conceded. “But he’s got stronger. He’s worked hard on that … And just for it to come together has been great.”

The Dodgers and San Francisco Giants kept things neck-and-neck through the first half of Saturday night’s contest, but the Dodgers rattled off six unanswered runs in a 10-4 victory.
After Tarik Skubal allowed a two-out walk to Giants designated hitter Victor Bericoto, Jung Hoo Lee attacked the first pitch he saw into the right-center field gap, but a diving play from Kyle Tucker got Skubal out of the inning with the game remaining scoreless.
Mookie Betts started things off in the bottom of the first inning with a leadoff double, and Max Muncy cashed him in with a two-strike, two-out RBI double to give the Dodgers the first lead of the game. Betts would come through again in the bottom of the second inning, lacing an RBI single the other way to plate Josue De Paula and make it a 2-0 Dodger lead.
Skubal worked his way around two baserunners for a scoreless top of the second inning, but after allowing a one-out single to Turner Hill in the top of the third inning, Bericoto launched a 3-2 fastball deep over the center field wall, tying the game at 2. Will Smith wasted no time giving the Dodgers the lead again, hammering a solo home run to lead off the bottom of the third inning, giving him his second home run in as many games.
The Giants responded with a pair of leadoff singles from Andrew Knizner and Osleivis Basabe to begin the top of the fourth inning. A bunt from Christian Koss moved both men into scoring position, and a squeeze bunt from Jonah Cox plated Knizner to tie the game at 3.
The Dodgers would get another one-run lead thanks to an RBI double from Mookie Betts in the bottom of the fourth inning— his second double and second RBI of the game. The Giants wouldn’t let Skubal settle in for the top of the fifth inning, as Bericoto and Lee both doubled to tie the game at four.
Saturday turned out to be Skubal’s worst outing of the season, let alone as a Dodger. Skubal managed to complete five innings of work but allowed a season-high four earned runs, while his three strikeouts on the night were the fewest in any start since striking out three on August 14 of last season against the Minnesota Twins.
Despite the poor start, the Dodgers put Skubal officially in line for the win as Teoscar Hernández ignited a two-out rally with an opposite-field single. Kyle Tucker and Josue De Paula each followed with a walk, and Tommy Edman snapped out of a 1-37 funk with a go-ahead, two-run single to give the Dodgers their first multi-run lead since the third. Miguel Rojas knocked a pinch-hit single to bring home De Paula, but Edman was thrown out at home attempting to make it a four-run inning.
Evan Phillips recorded the first clean inning of the night in relief of Skubal in the top of the sixth inning, and the Dodgers responded with another three-run inning, capitalized by a two-run single by De Paula and giving the Dodgers a six-run cushion.
After a scoreless inning from Alex Vesia in the seventh inning, Edwin Díaz came in for his second consecutive game since returning from injury, pitching a scoreless top of the eighth inning while picking up a pair of strikeouts.
Mookie Betts finished Saturday going 4-4 with three doubles and two RBI, reaching base five times after a walk in the seventh inning. Betts is now 10-12 (.833 average) over his last three games with three doubles, two home runs and five RBI.
With their win over the Giants, the Dodgers maintain a four-game lead over the Atlanta Braves for the no. 2 seed in the National League. They still trail the Milwaukee Brewers by two games for the top seed.

- Home runs— Victor Bericoto (5); Will Smith (9)
- WP— Tarik Skubal (11-7): 5 IP, 8 hits, 4 earned runs, 2 walks, 3 strikeouts
- LP— Yunior Marte (0-1): 4 2/3 IP, 8 hits, 6 earned runs, 3 walks, 2 strikeouts

The Dodgers wrap things up against San Francisco on Sunday (1:10 p.m. PT, SportsNet LA) before hosting the San Diego Padres for their final regular season home series beginning Tuesday. Both teams have yet to announce their starters.

LOS ANGELES — Andy Pages went through the paces on Saturday afternoon, grinding through an intense on-field workout in the clearest sign yet that he will be ready to return on Tuesday to open the final home series of the regular season.
Pages wore a fitness tracker, similar to what soccer players use to monitor all aspects of physical fitness. Coaches and staff put him through an estimated five simulated innings all in a compressed window of time.
The All-Star center fielder not only tested his broken left hand, but he also pushed his physical fitness to the limits.
Pages went from hitting to defense to base running and then doing it all over again to make sure he is ready for the rigors of play next week. His return is expected to come in the opener of a three-game series against the San Diego Padres.
While that kind of energy output is typically done in a rehab game, there aren’t many minor league options remaining this late in the season.
One thing Pages will not get is the chance to hit off a pitcher at full velocity.
“I think that from what I understand, we don’t have really any available arms,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said about the prospect of a live batting practice session. “A lot of our guys are playing in playoff games in the minors, and we have (Eric) Lauer, who’s on the IL. So, we don’t really have anyone.”
That’s not ideal for a player coming off the uncertainty that comes with a hand injury. But Pages did show that his hand soreness has subsided enough to hit multiple balls over the outfield wall.
“I’m expecting good at-bats,” Roberts said. “I can’t speak to the performance. I just want him to have good at-bats, and I’m not sure where he’s going to hit. Somewhere middle to the bottom (of the order), I think. I think I’m waiting just like you guys are waiting to see how it looks.”
The Dodgers close the season with six consecutive games, including the season-ending series in San Francisco next weekend.
“Six in a row, and that seems pretty aggressive (for Pages),” Roberts said. “So, I think that we do want to get him as many at-bats as possible, but we have to make sure that his legs are under him, feeling good, so we don’t go backward or get injured in that respect. It is going to be a balancing act and just keeping a keen eye on Andy, for sure.”
Regardless of what his swing looks like, the Dodgers still trust him in center field. After all, his World Series-saving catch in Game 7 last season came as a late-inning defensive replacement.
“Playing a premium position and playing it well is hugely important,” Roberts said.
ROTATING THE ROTATION
Left-hander Blake Snell is not expected to pitch in the upcoming series against the Padres, but he has not been ruled out for the series against the Giants next weekend.
Snell left his start Thursday after one inning in Cincinnati because of groin discomfort.
“He’s trending very well,” Roberts said about Snell’s recovery in recent days.
Right-hander Roki Sasaki is expected to pitch in the upcoming series against the Padres, although his role has not yet been specified. There is a chance Sasaki could start a game against San Diego, or come out of the bullpen, which had been his expected role in the postseason.
“It will be multiples for sure,” Roberts said about Sasaki’s innings count. “I just don’t know exactly when.”
A LEADING MAN
Shohei Ohtani is still expected to return to play before the regular season ends next Sunday, although there remains no target date.
In the meantime, the Dodgers continue to weigh their options in the leadoff spot. Tommy Edman was there immediately after Ohtani went on the injured list earlier this month, Josue De Paula took a turn there and Mookie Betts has been the latest to stake a claim.
Betts hit two home runs from the leadoff spot Friday and was back at the top of the lineup on Saturday.
“Yeah, I think that certainly there is an uncertainty with Shohei, all the while expecting him to be back,” Roberts said. “But you do got to kind of prepare for whatever, and I just think that Mookie’s swinging the bat well, has hit there many times throughout his career, so it just kind of makes sense.”
Betts had three hits Wednesday in Cincinnati and three more Friday against the Giants in the leadoff spot, including two home runs. He is batting .356 with six home runs and 18 RBIs in 15 September games.
ALSO
The Dodgers are expected to select a pitcher to pick up bulk innings on Sunday in a hybrid bullpen game against the Giants, but the exact plan remains undetermined.
UP NEXT
Giants (LHP Matt Wilkinson, 1-3, 4.58 ERA) at Dodgers (TBA), Sunday, 1:10 p.m., SportsNet LA, 570 AM, 1020 AM

- Mookie Betts hits three doubles and the Dodgers surge for 15 hits to overcome a shaky start by Tarik Skubal in a 10-4 win over the San Francisco Giants.
When Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said earlier this week that the best was yet to come, his expectations were centered on the offense.
In the Dodgers’ 10-4 rout of the San Francisco Giants on Saturday, that better version of the offense was on display, putting together a pair of three-run rallies in back-to-back innings to take pressure off the pitching staff.
Before that breakout started in the fifth inning, it was a back-and-forth game.
Dodgers left-handed starting pitcher Tarik Skubal pitched only five innings, tied for his shortest start with the Dodgers. And he surrendered four runs, the worst mark of his Dodgers tenure.
Tyler Glasnow hasn’t had the greatest of seasons, but the Dodgers will need him to deliver in the playoffs if they want to win another World Series title.
Entering the game, Skubal appeared to be peaking. His last two starts, both against the Reds, were some of his most efficient.
That efficiency, however, regressed against the Giants (64-91).
Though he got through the first two innings without giving up a run — thanks in part to a diving catch by right fielder Kyle Tucker made in the gap to end the first — he issued two-out walks in each.
The Dodgers’ offense used that time to mount a lead. Leadoff hitter Mookie Betts, who finished the day with three doubles and a single, hit the first of those doubles in his first at-bat, and Max Muncy authored his own to drive in the first run.
The next inning, rookie Josue De Paula’s walk, and singles from Alex Freeland and Betts combined to push in another run.
Then Skubal began to struggle. With a runner on second and one out, he pitched to a full count against designated hitter Victor Bericoto. Skubal missed down the middle with a fastball, and Bericoto sent it 425 feet to center field. It landed on the netting on the other side of the wall to tie the score.
The Dodgers’ offense, coming alive in September, struck back in the third. Catcher Will Smith hit his second home run in as many nights, launching the second pitch of the frame into left-field stands.
The Giants took a different approach to tie the score for a second time. After back-to-back singles, they used back-to-back sacrifice bunts to advance the runners and score another run.
Then the two teams traded runs again. Betts put the Dodgers (95-60) up with an RBI double in the fourth. Skubal gave up back-to-back doubles in the fifth.
That marked both the end of Skubal’s start and the beginning of the Dodgers’ offensive onslaught.
If the man trying to revive the Montreal Expos as an expansion team succeeds, Dan Evans is his choice for president of baseball operations.
The Dodgers brought seven batters to the plate in the fifth, and all but one reached base. Tommy Edman hit a two-run single. And pinch-hitting Miguel Rojas almost matched him, but Giants left fielder Turner Hill made a perfect throw to nab Edman in a close play at home to end the inning.
Betts’ and Smith’s bats stayed hot to open the sixth with a leadoff double and one-out RBI single, respectively. The Dodgers took advantage of the Giants’ sloppy infield play to load the bases for De Paula, who lined a two-run single into shallow center field.
Those were the kinds of stifling rallies that had defined the Dodgers offense earlier in the season, when they were scoring regularly in double digits.
The Dodgers’ 15 hits Saturday were their most in a game since July 2 against the San Diego Padres, and just two shy of their season high.

Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts addressed the team's lead-off position as Shohei Ohtani sits and Mookie Betts thrives.
The Shohei Ohtani lead-off question
On Saturday, September 19th, Roberts was asked directly whether Ohtani would lead off when he returned from the injured list, Dodgers Nation's Noel Sanchez reports.
"I mean, I think that's my first kind of thought," Roberts said to the media, including Dodgers Nation.
"But until he gets back, or when he gets back, then I'll kind of potentially read and react if it's a left-right situation. I haven't really thought too much about it."
Ohtani is on the IL with right arm/bicep soreness, which surfaced during his pitching work. He's also battling left knee soreness.
The Dodgers hope rest will help Ohtani, who looked like a shell of his best self in his last few at-bats before sitting out.
Over the last few days, Ohtani has been doing light baseball work and is trending in a good direction, according to Dave Roberts, leaving the door open for him to get some plate appearances before the postseason.
Why Ohtani may not lead off
As the Dodgers found out, a compromised Ohtani cannot touch the same heights as a fully healthy one. As the injuries racked up and the wear led to a hampered swing, Ohtani was not delivering at a level to merit the lead-off spot.
Ohtani hit just .186/.324/.390 in his last 15 games, with production looking really bad over the last seven games: .077 with a .250 OBP.
While Ohtani has dropped off, Mookie Betts has started heating up and is now taking over the leadoff spot in Ohtani's absence.
Mookie Betts is challenging Ohtani
For most of Ohtani's time out injured, which has been a few weeks now, Tommy Edman has handled most of the lead-off work.
However, Edman is now hitting .135/.274/.231 at lead-off, and Betts is really getting going.
Betts is hitting .356 with a .457 OBP over his last 15 games. Over 30 games, Betts is hitting .298/.384/.529.
Roberts talked about deploying Betts at leadoff for a second straight game, even against a righty pitcher
"I think that certainly there is uncertainty with Shohei, all the while expecting to be back. But you do have to prepare for whatever," Roberts said to the media, including Dodgers Nation.
"I just think Mookie swinging the bat well and has many times throughout his career. It just kind of makes sense."
If Betts keeps this up and Ohtani returns still limited, Roberts will have to think hard about moving the batting order to improve the team's three-peat odds.

The Los Angeles Dodgers could be getting one of their All-Stars back from injury. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts told Dodger Insider that Andy Pages will return when the club hosts the San Diego Padres.
It had been previously reported that Pages would return on the Dodgers’ final homestand of the 2026 season. This update gives a firmer timeline for when the 2026 All-Star will return to the lineup.
Pages has been a huge boost to the Dodgers’ lineup. The 25-year-old has slashed .272/.358/.458 with 21 home runs and a 119 wRC+ in 127 games this season. He also provides elite center field defense, rated at +18 Defensive Runs Saved and +9 Outs Above Average.
Dodgers Provide Andy Pages Return Timeline
With a return date set for Andy Pages, that means he’ll get roughly six games of action to prepare for the postseason. Ideally, the Dodgers center fielder can shake off a month’s worth of rust, since he won’t have the luxury of a rehab assignment.
Pages suffered a fracture of his left hand when he got hit by a 100 MPH fastball from the Pirates‘ Bubba Chandler. The club has turned to Alek Thomas and Tommy Edman in center field in his absence.
Edman is currently penciled in as the everyday center fielder after Thomas struggled in a short stint. The former Diamondback was later DFA’d, then outrighted to Triple-A after seven games in the lineup.
With Pages returning, the Dodgers have some tough lineup decisions. Edman will most likely return to the infield, bumping Alex Freeland off second base and off the roster. With Teoscar Hernandez on a hot streak, the club is unlikely to take him out of the lineup.
Dodgers Right Now
At 93-60, the Dodgers are currently up four games in the loss column over the Atlanta Braves, meaning they’re in great position to earn a bye for the Wild Card round.
They’ve already taken care of the first step by securing their fifth straight National League West division title. Now it’s just setting themselves up for the best chance to make a run in the postseason.
There are a lot of injuries the club needs to navigate. Shohei Ohtani, Roki Sasaki, and Edgardo Henriquez are the big ones to follow. Getting Ohtani back and healthy is going to be important if the Dodgers want to finish their three-peat bid.
Los Angeles will finish their 2026 season in California. They host the San Francisco Giants and San Diego Padres on their final homestand. Then they’ll finish out the year in San Francisco.
The Dodgers will send right-hander Tyler Glasnow for the series opener against the Giants. First pitch at Uniqlo Field at Dodger Stadium is set for 7:15 p.m. PT, with the game being broadcast on Apple TV+.

The Cuban had surgery on his broken hand shortly after, and he has since steadily increased his baseball activity.
When will Andy Pages return?
On Friday, September 18th, before the Dodgers’ home game against the Giants, Pages told AM 570’s David Vassegh he hopes to return for Tuesday’s game against the Padres.
Manager Dave Roberts has already told the media, including Dodgers Nation, that Pages would be activated at some point during the homestand.
The Dodgers will be home from Friday to Wednesday, before ending their regular season against the Giants in San Francisco.
If Pages does return on Tuesday, that would give him five games to get up to MLB game speed.
Assuming he rests one of those, Pages would have only four games to get everything clicking.
Why the Dodgers need Andy Pages back
Pages is an elite defender, with a 9.5 defensive rating, according to FanGraphs.
Tommy Edman, who has taken on the center field responsibilities, has -1 outs above average. While Pages has 8 outs above average at center field, according to Baseball Savant.
For a team that prides itself on defense, Pages presents the glove and range needed to help keep runs down and help the starting pitching stay in the game.
Pages has a 3.9 fWAR and a 119 wRC+ this season, and as a hitter, he brings a good bat-on-ball skill set.
On both ends of the field, Pages is invaluable to the Dodgers, and they will need him for the postseason.

The Los Angeles Dodgers begin their final homestand of the season on Friday night against the rival San Francisco Giants.
The Dodgers (93-60) clinched the National League West for the 13th time in the last 14 years on Thursday. The Giants (64-89) are a whopping 29 games behind LA in the division.
“It’s a big deal. It’s not easy,” manager Dave Roberts said of his team winning another NL West title. “I think a lot of people think it’s easy, it’s a rite of passage. But it’s not easy to win a division when everyone is gunning for you, to keep everyone motivated to play over the course of 162. It’s something we’re all really proud of. But that’s not the end goal.”
The Dodgers and Giants play six times over the next 10 days to close out the season. The Dodgers are just 3-4 against the Giants this season.
Dodgers vs Giants Pitching Matchup on Friday
Right-handed pitcher Tyler Glasnow is taking the ball for the Dodgers on Friday night amid a concerning stretch of play.
The right-hander has allowed four runs in each of his last two starts. After his most recent one, manager Dave Roberts somewhat ominously said Glasnow "didn’t feel great" going into it.
Glasnow has made four starts since coming off the IL after a four-month absence due to a back injury. He left the team to go home early this week instead of traveling with them to Cincinnati as the staff wanted to have him avoid going on two flights.
The Dodgers will hope for better results from him on Friday, especially after Blake Snell left his Wednesday start with a groin injury.
For what it's worth, Glasnow's best start of the season came against the Giants in April, when he allowed one hit over eight shutout innings with nine strikeouts.
Opposite Glasnow will be left-hander Cesar Perdomo, who owns a 3.68 ERA over 14.2 career innings at the MLB level.
He made his debut on Sept. 1 as a reliever before starting each of his last two games.

CINCINNATI — As the celebrating Los Angeles Dodgers drenched one another in various carbonated boozes, the team's most important character was bone dry and most likely quite sober roughly two thousand miles away.
Shohei Ohtani, that baseballing mover of mountains, is injured. A laundry list of ailing body parts — biceps, knee, neck — first kept the two-way dynamo from pitching, then frayed his offensive impact and finally rendered him physically incapable of taking the field. Last week, the Dodgers placed him on the IL, with just a few weeks left for him to recover before the start of the postseason and only five games between his earliest eligible return date and the end of the regular season.
Publicly, the club has maintained an optimistic tone, describing his issues as manageable, not season-ending. A return before the end of the regular season is still in play, skipper Dave Roberts reaffirmed this week. Yet nobody around the game would be shocked if the Dodgers opt for caution and keep Ohtani sidelined until October. Los Angeles' worst-case scenario, of course, would be a postseason without its main man.
So when the Dodgers embarked on their recent two-city swing, their $700 million slugger stayed back in Southern California. He rested, received treatment and hit off a tee — or, as Roberts vaguely put it, "continued his progression."
"Overall, [his] body feels normal-ish," Roberts said before Thursday's clincher. "Then it's kind of getting his body, his knee, his arm, biceps, whatever, back to full strength."
This marked the first time in the Dodgers' Ohtani Era that the man himself did not accompany the team for the entirety of a road trip. In fact, the most recent occurrence of a Dodgers club flying home without Ohtani came in October 2023, after the team's sweep loss to the Diamondbacks in that year's NLDS. Lance Lynn, Austin Barnes and a decade of frustration were on board that plane. Ohtani was still technically an Angel. In other words, it's been a while.
With the two-way superstar now the center of the Dodgers' solar system — and, to a large extent, the league's extended universe — Ohtani's absence this week in Cincinnati was easy to sense, impossible to avoid. Throughout the week, all about the yard, were reminders both big and small.
The blue bat bags lined up outside the locker room in numerical order went right from Will Smith's No. 16 to Kyle Tucker's No. 23, with no No. 17 to be found. Dodgers head security guard Al Garcia, typically within eyesight of Ohtani at all times, floated around the clubhouse with an uncharacteristically laid-back comportment buoyed by his relatively light list of duties.
A group of passionate Dodgers fans recognized the star's absence with a homemade sign that read "Feel Better Shohei, Give Decoy A Hug," making reference to Ohtani's dog. Even Yoshinobu Yamamoto admitted that it was odd not having Ohtani around, delivering one of his funnier and more cutting lines of the season.
"It's been a weird feeling because I talk to him all the time in the clubhouse," Yamamoto said via interpreter Yoshihiro Sonoda. "Although I have Roki [Sasaki], he doesn't really talk to me."
The Dodgers' lineup missed Ohtani, too, averaging less than four runs per game on the road trip before Thursday's eight-run outburst against a bottom-five Cincinnati pitching staff. Utilityman Tommy Edman got the bulk of leadoff duties, with Mookie Betts and rookie call-up Josue De Paula getting a day each in the one-hole. Edman went just 1-for-23 on the trip. Freddie Freeman's power dip continued, with five singles and nothing else. Will Smith has yet to really pop off since his return from the IL on Sept. 1.
"It feels different because he's such a presence when he's on the field," Roberts admitted Monday.
Therein lies the lingering concern. The Dodgers and Ohtani have all but accepted that he won't pitch again this season. That's not the end of the world; Los Angeles has the arms to solve that problem. On the other hand, navigating October without Ohtani at full-go would be a difficult proposition.
Ohtani's health, too, is not binary. Even if he plays, which at this point feels likely, he's unlikely to be completely healed. That dynamic could very well hamper his performance. Ohtani, overly cautious as they come, revealed that concern the last time he spoke to reporters on Sept. 8.
"I should have enough experience to address any kinks or injuries or anything like that with the swing," Ohtani said. "I'm going to use this as an opportunity to add on to the experience that I've had previously and address it regardless."
It's not exactly the most reassuring explanation — Ohtani implying that he'll need to manage his various discomforts for the rest of the season. How that process transpires and how productive Ohtani proves to be in October could determine how many Champagne celebrations he'll get to participate in this year.

Welcome to Waiver Wire Watch, our weekly fantasy baseball waiver wire guide. We’ll be doing things a little differently this season, with James Schiano publishing the initial waiver-wire article on Friday afternoon. Then Eric Samulski updates it every Sunday to make sure you get the most up-to-date information.
We’re doing things a little bit differently this time of year though. Rather than give a long list of players with deep analysis, there will only be a few dense player profiles for those we think currently need a bit more light shed on them. Otherwise, there will be long lists of players who can help your teams in a specific category or for this particular week.
The premise of the article is pretty straightforward. We’ll give you some recommended adds each week based on recent production or role changes. When we list a player, we’ll list the category where we think he’ll be helpful or the quick reason he’s listed. We hope this helps you determine whether the player fits your team’s needs. Not every “trending” player will be a good addition to your specific roster.
To qualify for this list, a player needs to be UNDER 40% rostered in Yahoo! formats. We understand you may say, “These players aren’t available in my league,” and we can’t help you there. These players are available in over 60% of leagues and some in 98% of leagues, so they’re available in many places, and that can hopefully satisfy readers who play in all league types.
